note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 166 to 184 - Cavendish Road South, Holles Crescent, Lenton Road, Park Drive and Tattershall Drive.** Transcribed by A. Hagues. **This block closes the round**: with it, every schedule from 1 to 261 is in the record but schedule 51, whose head sits on a sheet that has not been read.

**Two William Vickers, father and son, two doors apart.** **William Vickers senior, 83, magistrate and proprietor**, at 4 Lenton Road with his wife Mary, 81 - and **William Vickers junior, 58, manufacturer**, at 6 Lenton Road with his own family. The enumerator writes "Sen" and "Jun" to keep them apart, and this file does the same with a birth year on each.

**Cavendish Road South is a street the record has no properties on at all**, and the page puts five households on it - including **Howard A Allport**, a civil engineer and colliery proprietor, and **John Manning, Alderman and magistrate**, whose family the record already knows from Lenton Road forty years later. **Hucknall Lodge** is the only house on it the page names. See [[cavendish-road-south-has-no-properties]].

**Holles Crescent is given three times and numbered none.** One of the three has no head at all - two servants and nobody to serve.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source. Repeated names carry a birth year and are matched on it.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book RG11/3367, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 166 to 184, transcribed by A. Hagues.
